key_insight: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials can automate crystallographic plausibility checks, but their error-detection performance is model-dependent and incomplete.
engineering_relevance: MLIP-based relaxation offers a scalable screening layer for large crystal databases like COD, helping flag suspect structures faster than manual expert review.
method: Filtered 522,086 COD entries to 317,457 high-quality structures.
Relaxed structures with M3GNet and compared deposited vs relaxed volumes and convergence behavior.
Benchmarked M3GNet, CHGNet, PET-MAD, and PET-OAM on 524 manually selected cases with known or suspected errors.
evidence_signal: Among filtered entries, 314,153 of 317,457 structures converged with little volume change, while manual review of 327 structures showed no single threshold cleanly separated valid from invalid structures.
watch_item: Do not rely on one MLIP alone: models fail differently on motifs such as π ligands and heterocycles, so multi-model screening is safer than a single-model decision.
paper_title: Assessing the Reliability of Foundational Machine Learning Potentials for Evaluating the Veracity of the Crystallography Open Database
